description: Critical Minerals Atlas is a free web map and set of dashboards that trace critical mineral supply chains site by site, locating mines, concentrators, refineries, smelters, manufacturers and market hubs. At access it had full dashboards for 22 of 60 planned minerals, including antimony, cobalt, lithium, rare earths, tungsten, copper and nickel. It is built and maintained by an independent developer, Nick Raineri, from public sources such as the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, US government finance and defence agencies, the Department of Energy and company filings of operators such as MP Materials and Lynas. Coverage is global but uneven: deepest for Africa, the Americas and the US industrial base, thin for Russia and Central Asia; the beta version 11 was updated on 11 September 2026. It is free, with no registration, tracking or cookies; the page read states no licence and there is no bulk download. Caveats: it is a one-person work in progress described as a plain-language primer, so completeness and verification vary and corrections are invited. For simulation it gives node locations and roles for supply chain network models of critical minerals, useful for tracing how the loss of a mine, smelter or port would cascade to manufacturers, and for overlaying sites with hazards. It is related to the World Bank Pink Sheet record in this catalogue, which gives the prices of the same commodities.
